parts.title: Basil Lost a Race to a SNAIL! Which Fix Works? | What Is a System? | P4 Science
parts.description:
Basil is sure that LIGHTER IS FASTER, so he takes the bell, the chain and the brakes off his bike before racing Uncle Lim round the void deck. Pigeons, a snail and a runaway bike later, it's three minutes to the race. Pick the fix: pedal faster, put back all three parts, or put back only the chain and the brakes? Then watch every fix get tested.

In this video:
• The problem: Basil in an ice box
• Pick the fix: 1, 2 or 3?
• Ten minutes earlier: the bell, the chain and the brakes
• The runaway bike!
• The race (and a twist)
• Look closer: every part has a function
• Be a link of a bike chain: the parts interact
• Putting it back together: what is a system?
• Your body and a tree are systems too
• The words that earn marks
• Stay for the blooper after the end!

Key words: function, interact, system.
The words that earn marks: A system is made up of different parts. Each part has its own function. The parts interact to perform a function. When one part stops working, the whole system is likely to be affected.

For parents: this is a story, not a lecture. Children pick a fix with their fingers before each idea is tested, so they think before they are told. It opens the Systems theme of Primary 4 Science (Singapore Primary Science Syllabus 2023). A common mistake it fixes: "if one part breaks, everything stops". The syllabus says the whole system is "likely" to be affected: a bike with no bell still moves, but less safely. Also fits US NGSS 4-LS1-1 (Grade 4: structures that work together).
Try it (with an adult): turn a bicycle upside down, turn a pedal by hand, and watch the chain turn the back wheel. Then check the brakes and the bell. Ride safely; check your brakes.

TheOneApp, Explained: Singapore primary science, made fun. Play along with Pip, Basil and Momo: show fingers to lock in, keep score on your hand, beat the Buddies!
